Subject: Clarification on SLA measurement for RFP item 4.2 (uptime & latency)

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the rapid turnaround on the RFP. Procurement and our infra team reviewed section 4.2 and have a handful of clarifying questions before we can proceed to legal:

- How do you define monthly uptime (calendar month vs 30-day rolling)?
- What latency SLOs do you apply to text-generation endpoints (p50/p95/p99) and how are tokens factored into measurement?
- Describe the measurement methodology and the canonical data source in disputes (customer-side probes, Redwood telemetry, third-party monitoring?).
- How are scheduled maintenance windows accounted for (notification window, maximum frequency/duration)?
- Please provide an example calculation for a service credit and the cap on credits as a percent of monthly fees.

If you can provide a signed appendix or an official response we can attach to the RFP, that would speed up procurement. I attached the RFP excerpt for reference (not included here).

Best,
Alice

Globex Corp
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarification on SLA measurement for RFP item 4.2 (uptime & latency)

Alice —

Thanks for the clear list. Below is a consolidated response we typically provide to enterprise RFPs; I've attached an editable appendix and a latency sampling spreadsheet for your team to review. High-level answers first, then a short walk-through of measurement.

High-level commitments (standard offering):
- Uptime: 99.95% availability measured per calendar month (UTC).
- Latency SLOs (text-generation API, baseline 256-token request): p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 650ms. These are averages across requests served on our standard hosted tier and are measured server-side.
- Service credits: percentage of monthly invoice proportional to the shortfall beneath the uptime target (see attached SLA_Appendix_v3.pdf). Max cumulative credits cap at 50% of the monthly service fees.

Measurement methodology (summary):
- Canonical source: Redwood server-side telemetry exported to our metrics pipeline (Datadog). For disputes we propose: first compare Redwood telemetry, then a reconciliation run against customer-provided probe data and, if still in dispute, an agreed third-party measurement (see arbitration section in appendix).
- Sampling: p99 computed using 1-minute aggregated buckets across regional clusters. Each bucket records request counts and latency histograms; percentiles are calculated on the aggregated histograms for the measurement window.
- Token normalization: SLOs are defined for a 256-token request baseline. Requests with longer generation lengths are normalized according to our token-latency model (spreadsheet attached) — this is how we compare like-for-like.
- Measurement window: calendar month, reporting in UTC. A short outage is considered continuous if gaps exceed 2 minutes of failed request responses; brief jitter under that threshold is treated as latency degradation, not total downtime.

Maintenance & exclusions:
- Scheduled maintenance: we provide 72-hour advance notice for planned maintenance windows. Up to 4 hours/month of scheduled maintenance (or pre-announced longer windows that are mutually agreed) are excluded from uptime calculations. Emergency maintenance will be excluded if we provide an after-action report.
- Exclusions include customer misconfigurations, third-party upstream outages (cloud provider), DDoS where we can demonstrate traffic origination external to our protections, and force majeure.

Service credit example (see CSV):
- If monthly uptime is 99.85% (0.10% below target) we apply a credit equal to X% of the monthly bill (detailed tiers in the appendix). Credits are issued on the following billing cycle after validation.

Next steps: If Globex is comfortable, sign the attached SLA_Appendix_v3.pdf (editable) and we can lock terms into the master services agreement. Happy to jump on a short call to walk through the latency spreadsheet with your infra team.

Cheers,

Sean Gallagher
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: SLA_Appendix_v3.pdf; latency_sampling_protocol.xlsx; service_credit_calc_example.csv

Sean —

Appreciate the quick response and the attachments. A few follow-ups from infra/procurement:

1) Can you confirm the monthly uptime excludes scheduled maintenance only if notice provided >=72 hours AND window is logged in the appendix? Our security team wants the audit trail.
2) For the arbitration clause, can Redwood accept Datadog (your exported metrics) as the authoritative source provided both parties have access to the metrics export? Globex would like an option to ingest a read-only export into our monitoring for independent verification.
3) For the token-normalization model: will Redwood share the normalization coefficients and the sample dataset used to derive them? Our performance team wants to reproduce the normalization locally.

If you can add these clarifications to the appendix we can route to legal. Also, is there a maximum frequency for scheduled maintenances you can commit to (we'd prefer not to see repeated monthly windows >4hrs).

Thanks,
Alice

Subject: Re: SLA & Latency Sampling — Globex RFP follow-up

Alice — quick technical note on arbitration and exports: 

- We can provide a daily exported metrics bundle (Datadog-compatible JSON/CSV) for the previous 90 days to an agreed S3 bucket with read-only access for Globex. That export will include request counts, success/failure rates, latency histograms, and the token-normalization coefficients CSV used for SLO calculations.
- In the event of a dispute, our standard flow is: (1) compare Redwood's Datadog-derived numbers vs Globex probe data; (2) if mismatch remains, trigger a reconciliation job that re-runs percentile calculations over the raw histograms; (3) if still unresolved, bring in an agreed third-party (we typically use an independent monitoring vendor or an appointed auditor).
- We are comfortable naming Datadog-based exports as the canonical telemetry source for operational reconciliation, provided both parties accept the export schedule and access controls (we've included a draft access policy in the appendix).

Regarding maintenance frequency: we will not schedule more than one non-emergency maintenance window that exceeds 4 hours in any single calendar quarter for a given customer without explicit consent. Smaller windows (<= 4 hours) remain possible once/month but will not be used for disruptive infra upgrades unless notified.

Happy to add verbatim language to the appendix if you want it for legal.

—Karthik
Principal SRE — Redwood Inference

Alice —

Per Karthik's note I've updated the appendix to include:
- Explicit maintenance notification and audit-trail requirements (72-hour notice, S3-backed maintenance log).
- Statement that Redwood will provide daily Datadog-compatible exports (90-day retention) to a mutually agreed S3 bucket; export schema attached in the latency spreadsheet.
- Token-normalization coefficients and the sample dataset (anonymized) included in latency_sampling_protocol.xlsx.
- Maintenance frequency commitment: no more than one >4h scheduled maintenance per customer per quarter; up to 4h/month allowed for routine, non-disruptive work.

I've attached SLA_Appendix_v3.pdf with these clarifications and a short sample credit calculation table in service_credit_calc_example.csv. To move to procurement/legal we typically ask for a signed Appendix and then we populate the master services agreement. I've included a DocuSign link for the Appendix in related links.

If Globex wants an alternate canonical telemetry provider listed, tell us which vendor and we'll include them in the reconciliation clause.

Thanks,
Sean
